steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, white balsamic vinegar, garlic, and mustard powder. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Stir in minced fresh herbs if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This recipe has the perfect ingredients and the perfect measurements for whipping up the perfect vinaigrette made with white balsamic vinegar. Mix in some chopped fresh herbs if you wish.
raw_recipe.name: Balsamic Vinaigrette

recipeInstructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, white balsamic vinegar, garlic, and mustard powder. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Stir in minced fresh herbs if desired.

review.reviewBody: This is a wonderful recipe. After reading other people's reviews, I decided I needed to add something to sweeten it up. So I took two table spoons of honey, instead of sugar. I also used usual balsamic vinegar and didn't add any herbs so that I can enjoy just the taste of vinegar, black pepper and garlic. Turned out great! My boyfriend commented that this dressing makes him wants to keep eating salad.

This is a very good start, but I added a minced Shallot, a tablespoon of Honey and I cut the Balsamic Vinegar to 1/4 cup. Taste it, if you like it with more of any of the ingredients, add it and taste again. I adjusted it to how we like it, it was outstanding!

I'm sure it's good as written but...I only had 1/3 C olive oil, so added 1/4 C white balsamic and tblsp fresh lemon juice. Had poupon style mustard. Used fresh crushed garlic. added in 1 tsp of pulverized dried Italian seasoning and 1/2 tsp dried minced onion + 1 tsp Mirin (sweet cooking wine). Also, for elmusifiing I used 1 tsp mayo. I had a cleaned out "squeeze bear" honey comes in and shook it up in that. Tasted seriously good. Need to buy more olive oil so I can make larger quantity for summer time salads (with or without lettuce). Would be excellent marinade too or for pasta/potato salads for cookouts. Easy, quick and look forward to making with fresh herbs in summer. I made early in day so flavors married together.
This was fantastic! I did add about 2T honey to add a bit of substance and sweetness. Perfect on a mixed green salad with strawberries, mozzarella cheese pearls, honey roasted pecans. YUM!

This is a terrific and easy to make salad dressing. I have an old salad dressing carafe with lines on it showing the ratio of oil to vinegar, and a splash of water, which I added. As other reviewers stated, the balsamic vinegar needs to be a good quality, but it also needs a sweetener to balance it out. I used between 1-2 tablespoons of good quality raw honey, to taste. I may add a dash of Dijon mustard next time, but this is great not only for salads, but as a light sauce for steamed vegetable, pasta, even on chicken.
I followed all the directions but after reading some reviews I decided to add two tablespoons of honey for some sweetness. My family loves it and it turned out great!
I cut the vinegar to 1/3 cup and added 1 T. honey. It got rave reviews at the dinner I took the salad to!

This is a great recipe! I used regular balsamic vinegar and regular yellow mustard, and like others recommended, I added 2 tbsp honey and 1/2 tsp sugar to reduce the tartness. I blended this in my Magic Bullet blender, and the result was a restaurant quality dressing! Thanks for sharing!
Added a few basil leaves. 1/4 cup of olive oil and 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar. 1 garlic clove, 1/2 tsp ground mustard. Salt and pepper.

This is my kind of vinaigrette. It's easy to tweak to your taste. I love balsamic, however, I thought this could benefit from a little sugar. I used a good quality white balsamic, and extra virgin olive oil. Knowing I love garlic, I used a heaping 1/2 tsp. of garlic and 1 heaping tablespoons of white sugar. Dry mustard, kosher salt, and fresh cracked pepper fnished it off. This is light, slightly tangy and a perfect compliment to Italian dishes. I was looking for a good white balsamic vinaigrette and I'm gladly stopping here!

I made the recipe exactly as stated, but it was quite sour. I don't like sweet salad dressings, but this was too tart even for my taste buds. I added 2 tbsp raw honey, and it was perfect. With this addition I will make it again and again!
Used 1/4 c white balsamic. and 1 tbsp honey-didn't measure.

I’ve been using this recipe for a few years and love it. The other day I added in honey as many of the commenters suggested and they were right - - it definitely elevated the dressing! Thanks to all of you
This was very 'okay'. I will not be making it again. The flavor was mild/bland for us with a strong vinegar flavor. Thank you for the recipe.

I reduced the servings to 2 and put this on a sliced tomato. It was very good. The vinaigrette I use for summer cucumbers is similar but with the addition of a little sugar so I did put a pinch in this one. Afterward I read some reviews that other people did the same. I imagine it might be a little too vinegary without it.
This dressing is very tasty. I had to add about 2T of honey as it was just too vinegary.
This was slap your mama good. I made it exactly as written I will be making this often.
So simple and so delicious!

This is one of my basic go-to vinegarettes. I enjoy the tartness, probably because of the time I spent in Europe where the use of refined sugar is far less than here, so I don't add any sweetening agent. I sometimes use both sherry vinegar and white balsamic vinegar. A decent extra virgin olive oil (not the cheap stuff) is pretty essential, but a good olive oil will work. Both a quality dry mustard and fresh garlic make a big difference in taste. Because this dressing is so simple, adding or changing different herbs and spices to change the flavor is easy.
My husband made the dressing with out the shallots. I gave him many compliments. Very easy, very tasty.
